clue.text: First-class traveller in vehicle coming back

indicators.note: coming back means the whole combination is read from end to start
one thing sitting in another means the first is placed inside the second

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
a rep is a travelling sales representative

explanation.surface: A first-class passenger in a car or coach that is returning home.
explanation.walkthrough: A rep is a travelling salesperson; 'coming back' applies to the whole combination after the insertion, not just the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb is an adjective of praise meaning excellent, just as first-class is.

clue.text: Naively accepts birds of passage

definitions.meaning: first meaning: believes something without question
second meaning: migratory birds that fly south each autumn

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about gullibility, but it splits into a verb and a plural noun sharing one spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow a story is to believe it credulously, and swallows are well-known migrant birds.

clue.text: Devoutness shown by type I converted

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Religious devotion displayed by a person who has been converted to a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' fits the religious surface perfectly, which hides its job as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is religious devotion and reverence, the same quality devoutness names.

clue.text: Study before college in US to get let in again

indicators.note: before places the first word's letters ahead of the second's

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A student studies before attending an American college in order to be allowed back in.
explanation.definitionFit: To readmit someone is to allow them entry once more.

clue.text: Device in kitchen occupying more space, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: something larger occupies more space

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget that takes up too much room on the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A grater is a kitchen utensil for shredding cheese or vegetables.

clue.text: Finish in arena that's producing tears

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: a boxing or circus ring is an arena
end is a synonym of finish

explanation.surface: An emotional ending in a stadium that leaves the crowd crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' suggests crying, but here it means rips, rhyming with 'bears'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rending means tearing apart, so it is producing rips in cloth.

clue.text: Retaliation as result of change of heart

parts.words: Retaliation as result of change of heart
parts.note: surface reading: someone hits back after changing their mind
setter's reading: change the middle letter of a small bird's name from I to A and the bird is swapped for a scrap of cloth

explanation.walkthrough: Swap the heart of TIT for an A and you get TAT, so one is exchanged for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for repaying an injury with a like injury, which is retaliation.

clue.text: Celebrate holding a show

indicators.note: holding means the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: to revel is to celebrate
taken as written

explanation.surface: Throwing a party while putting on a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a noun, a performance, but it is the verb meaning to disclose.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to disclose or expose, which is to show.

clue.text: Finally looked at variety of maple or other tree

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters take a new order
finally points to the closing letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the last letter of looked
taken as written
the letters of maple rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone examines a kind of maple or some different species of tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety' sounds botanical, as in a cultivar of maple, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The date palm is a fruit-bearing tree, a different tree from a maple.

clue.text: The old lady hanging around, presenting spurious complaint

parts.note: 'old lady' is slang for mother, MA
lingering means staying on, hanging about

explanation.surface: An elderly woman loitering and making up an illness to get attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Malingering is faking or exaggerating illness to avoid work or duty.

clue.text: Local putting it back in centre of church

indicators.note: putting something back here means turning it end to end
in places the turned word inside the other

parts.note: the nave is the main central body of a church
it, turned round

explanation.surface: A villager returns an item to the middle of the parish church.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is a person from the area, which is what a native is.

clue.text: Make a killing with capital I extracted from Scottish island

indicators.note: something extracted is pulled out and taken away

parts.note: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides, famous for whisky
the capital letter I

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fortune by extracting capital from a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a killing' suggests profit and 'capital' money, but the definition is literal and the capital is just an upper-case letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To slay is to kill, so it is to make a killing taken literally.

clue.text: Agitated till our MP pens article with numerous extreme points

indicators.note: pens means encloses, as a fence holds sheep
agitated means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A worried local MP writes about something with many sharp tips.
explanation.definitionFit: Multipolar describes something having many poles, the extreme points of an axis or field.

clue.text: Following first eleven — almost time for play

parts.note: the position after the first eleven is the twelfth
nigh means nearly
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Sounds like a cricket team's twelfth man nearly getting a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First eleven' evokes a sports team; here it is simply counting to the next number.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelfth Night is a Shakespeare comedy, so it is a play.

clue.text: Fruit easy to transport that's sought by celebrity

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit
something light is easy to carry

explanation.surface: Portable fruit that a famous person craves.
explanation.definitionFit: The limelight is public attention, which celebrities are said to seek.

clue.text: A Republican state, or another

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican
Kansas is a US state

explanation.surface: A political label for one American state, or perhaps for another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' does double duty in spirit: it gives one US state, and 'another' defines a second state that the pieces build.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkansas is a different US state from Kansas, so it is another one.

clue.text: Doctor, the right kind, who knows best?

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
the nature of something is its kind or sort

explanation.surface: Asking which doctor is the right sort, the one who knows best.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'Mother knows best', applied to the natural world.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother Nature is the personified natural world, proverbially wiser than human meddling.

clue.text: Pressure good type to go into bank as better adviser

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it

parts.note: a tier is a bank or row, as of seats
P is the symbol for pressure
a saint is a good person, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: Someone is pressed to put money into a bank to become a better financial adviser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like the comparative of good, but here it means a person who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster gives racing tips, advising those who place bets.

clue.text: Person having no reason to butt heads with cabinet

parts.note: to nut someone is British slang for headbutting them
a case is a display cabinet

explanation.surface: An unreasonable person clashing with members of the government cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' suggests ministers, but it is a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutcase is informal for a crazy person, someone who has lost their reason.

clue.text: Show me up with superior ornament, in a way

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: me, turned round
a boss is one's superior at work

explanation.surface: An instruction to embarrass me in front of my manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show me up' reads as an idiom for embarrass; only 'up' does any work, turning the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: To emboss is to decorate a surface with raised designs, one particular way to ornament it.

clue.text: Details of contract quickly move around shopping area

indicators.note: around means the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: to sprint is to run fast
a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A hurried dash through a retail centre while reading a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Small print is the fine detail of a contract, often hiding unfavourable terms.

clue.text: Rabbit caught by bowler, say

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a bowler is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: A cricket image: a rabbit, a hopeless batsman, caught out by the bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to rabbit (on) is to talk at length; a bowler is a hard round hat as well as a cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbit is British slang for talk or chatter, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork'.

clue.text: Island that's cold most of month

indicators.note: most of means all but the final letter is kept

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold
April is a month

explanation.surface: An island where it is chilly for much of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian island in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Stop thinking about supporting contract

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
to contract an illness is to get it

explanation.surface: Advice to put a contract you backed out of your mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun, an agreement, but it is the verb meaning to catch.
explanation.definitionFit: To forget something is to cease to think of it.

clue.text: One holding up bar in part of India left job

parts.note: Goa is a state in western India
L is the abbreviation for left
a post is a job

explanation.surface: Someone propping up a bar in India who has quit work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding up bar' suggests a drinker propping up a pub counter; the bar is a crossbar.
explanation.definitionFit: Each upright goalpost supports the crossbar of a goal.

clue.text: Tries a novel, such as Gulliver's Travels

indicators.note: novel means new and original, so the letters take a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone attempts writing a book in the style of Swift's famous tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' suits a book clue as a noun but works as the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift's Gulliver's Travels is a classic example of satire, mocking politics and human folly.

clue.text: King and I having views about succession

indicators.note: about means going round the other pieces

parts.note: someone who sees has a view
R is Rex, Latin for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch and the speaker hold opinions about who inherits the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succession' hints at royal heirs, but it means a sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: A series is a number of things following one another in order, a succession.
